*   When multiple fall-through case clauses each have trailing line comments and the last such clause is followed by a block statement, all trailing comments must be preserved on their original case lines in the formatted output.

*   The formatter must be idempotent for this pattern: formatting the already-formatted output of such a switch statement a second time must produce exactly the same result as the first format pass.

*   This correct comment placement must apply in both 2-space and tab indentation modes.

The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

The implementation is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Problem

Biome's JS formatter was not idempotent for `switch` statements where a case clause has a trailing line comment and its body is a block statement:

```js
switch (x) {
  case 1: // comment a
  case 2: // comment b
  {
    doStuff();
  }
}
```

**Pass 1** produced `case 2: { // comment b` (comment floated onto the hugging block's brace line), and **Pass 2** then moved it to `case 2: {` / `// comment b` on its own line inside the block — a different result, and the comment was pulled into the block statement.

## Root cause

The trailing line comment after the colon is attached as a **trailing comment of the `test` expression** (e.g. the number literal `2`). Biome renders trailing line comments as a **line suffix**, which defers them to the next line break. When the block statement is allowed to *hug* the case line (`case 2: {`), the next line break occurs *inside* the block, so the comment floats into it.

## Fix

In `crates/biome_js_formatter/src/js/auxiliary/case_clause.rs`, I suppress the block-hugging behavior when the case's `test` expression carries a trailing line comment (`has_trailing_line_comment`). The clause then takes the existing non-hugging (`indent` + `hard_line_break`) branch, so the line-suffix comment flushes at the break right after the colon — keeping it on the case line:

```js
switch (x) {
  case 1: // comment a
  case 2: // comment b
    {
      doStuff();
    }
}
```

This is stable across passes (idempotent) in both 2-space and tab modes.
